en.headline: Customs seizes 7.5 kg cannabis buds at airport; Mainland woman arrested
en.dek: Officers found the suspected drugs, valued at about HK$1.5 million, inside the check-in baggage of a 31-year-old passenger who arrived from Bangkok via Taiwan on Friday.
body: Hong Kong Customs on Friday detected a drug trafficking case at Hong Kong International Airport and seized about 7.5 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of about HK$1.5 million.

A 31-year-old Mainland female passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, via Taiwan. During customs clearance, officers found the batch of suspected cannabis buds inside her check-in baggage. She was subsequently arrested.

An investigation is ongoing. Customs said it would continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking through intelligence analysis and risk assessment, focusing on passengers from high-risk regions.

Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence carrying a maximum penalty of a HK$5 million fine and life imprisonment. The department reminded the public not to carry unknown items for others or accept requests to transport controlled goods.

zh.headline: 海關機場檢7.5公斤大麻花拘內地女子 市值約150萬元
zh.dek: 一名31歲內地女旅客周五從曼谷經台灣抵港，寄艙行李藏懷疑大麻花被檢獲，她隨即被捕。
body: 香港海關周五在香港國際機場偵破一宗行李藏毒案件，檢獲約7.5公斤懷疑大麻花，估計市值約150萬元。
一名31歲內地女旅客當日從泰國曼谷經台灣抵港。海關人員在清關時於其寄艙行李內發現該批懷疑大麻花，隨即拘捕該名女子。
案件仍在調查中。海關表示會繼續根據情報分析及風險管理，重點檢查來自高風險地區的旅客，加強打擊跨境販毒活動。
根據《危險藥物條例》，販運危險藥物屬嚴重罪行，一經定罪最高可被判罰款500萬元及終身監禁。海關呼籲市民切勿為他人攜帶來歷不明物品或受管制物品進出香港。
